report.summary: Codex device-code login is added end to end: protocol schema, fixtures and generated Rust types; CredentialDO start/poll/cancel; server functions and registry; web Logins tab; Mac Settings; and spec updates to 01, 02, 04 and 07 in the same PR. CredentialDO keeps one attempt in memory per owner and runs start and poll one at a time. A cancel, removal or manual upload stops an attempt, including an in-flight exchange. Tokens are encrypted before saving and never appear in errors. Upstream requests have time limits and honor the poll interval. Worker tests use vitest-pool-workers and, with the UI tests, cover the main paths. Typecheck, lint and tests were not run (read-only review). No blocking issues found; three minor UX notes.

findings.text: upload_codex clears the auth.json input before SetCodexAuth returns. If the call fails (for example VALIDATION_FAILED), the owner has to paste the file again. Consider clearing it only on success.

The Mac Codex card shows only Set / Not set. 04 says each login shows set or not set and last updated; the web row shows updatedAt and lastRefresh. 07 says Logins should be the same on both, so the Mac version falls short.

Any non-pending upstream error during polling (such as a single 5xx) clears the attempt, so the client has to start a new login and get a new code. This matches the spec's wording but is unforgiving of brief upstream errors. Consider keeping the attempt on 5xx.
